stemMd: A laboratory wants to identify which of two filters removes more dust. It will compare the dust remaining downstream of each filter while the same volume of air passes through them. Which additional condition is needed for that comparison to isolate filter effectiveness?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The filters must cost the same amount.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The filters must have the same colour.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Both filters must be manufactured in the same town.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The downstream air must be completely dust-free.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The incoming air must contain the same amount of dust for both filters.

explanationMd: Equal air volume does not ensure equal dust exposure. If one filter receives cleaner air, less downstream dust might reflect the input rather than removal. Controlling the incoming dust amount closes that alternative explanation.

distractorRationale.b: Colour need not affect dust removal.
distractorRationale.c: Manufacturing location does not control the dust load.
distractorRationale.d: Perfect removal is not required to compare effectiveness.
distractorRationale.a: Price is irrelevant to the stated performance comparison.
